endpoints.title: Get Asset Labels
endpoints.description:
Lists the organization's asset entity labels for a category. `:category` is one of
`manufacturer`, `device_model`, `device_type`, `status`. Returns `{ items: [{ id, name }] }`.

On Create/Update Asset, each of these label fields accepts either the returned `{ "id": ... }`
or a plain name string (e.g. `"manufacturer": "Sony"`) — a name is resolved to an existing
label or a new one is created for the organization.

endpoints.title: Get Device
endpoints.description:
## Success
**200 OK** — a single device object.
```json
{
  "id": "1ad4e4e4-99b4-...",
  "name": "DSP-X200",
  "sn": "5pOLfS-...",
  "mac": null,
  "cloud_id": "...",
  "status": "online",
  "effective_status": "ok",
  "merged_effective_status": "ok",
  "last_seen_at": "2024-07-29T10:18:39.267Z",
  "details": null,
  "state": {},
  "model": { "id": "...", "name": "DSP-X200", "sub_model": null },
  "firmware": { "version": "1.0.0" },
  "space": { "id": 16138, "full_path": "Green Energy Corp/United Kingdom/London/Executive Suite" },
  "connector": { "type": "native", "id": null, "name": null },
  "maintenance": {
    "manual": { "active": false, "source": null },
    "scheduled": { "active": true, "until": "2026-10-21T04:00:00Z" }
  }
}
```
### Status fields
- `status` — the device's own raw self-reported state (`online` / `offline` / `unavailable` / `error`).
- `effective_status` — the device's own computed status: one of `ok`, `offline`, `error`, `warning`, `disconnected`, `never_seen`.
- `merged_effective_status` — merge-aware rollup of `effective_status` across the device group (primary + merged shadows), maintained on the group primary's row. On every other row — standalone or merged shadow — it mirrors that device's own `effective_status`.
- `connector` — `{ type, id, name }`: `type` is `native`, `c2c` or `edge`; `id` is the cloud connector or Edge id and `name` its display name (e.g. `Poly Lens`), `null` for native devices.

### Maintenance
- `maintenance.manual.active` — the device is in manual maintenance (its own incidents snoozed, or its space in maintenance).
- `maintenance.manual.source` — `device_snooze` when the device's own snooze is active, else `space` when its space is in maintenance, else `null`.
- `maintenance.scheduled.active` — a scheduled maintenance window covers the device's space now (see Maintenance Schedules); `maintenance.scheduled.until` is when it ends, `null` when none is active. Indication only: it does not change `status` or `effective_status`.

## Custom parameters (edge devices only)
For edge devices, the response includes a `custom_parameters` object — the device's current custom parameter values keyed by the field's human-readable label. This mirrors the `custom_parameters` object accepted by **Update Device**, so the object round-trips: read it, edit it, send it back. The field is omitted entirely for non-edge devices.

- **Password-type** parameters are never echoed back: a set password is masked as `"*****"`, and an unset password is returned as an empty string `""`.
- Non-password parameters with **no value set** are returned as `null`.

```json
{
  "custom_parameters": {
    "SNMP community": "public",
    "Port": "161",
    "Password": "*****"
  }
}
```

endpoints.title: Get Devices
endpoints.description:
## Query parameters
- `page` — page number (default `1`).
- `per_page` — results per page (default `100`, **max `100`**). Values above `100` are rejected with `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
- `space_id` — optional, filter to a single space.
- `name` — optional, case-insensitive substring match on the device name.
- `status` — optional, raw status: one or more of `online`, `offline`, `unavailable`, `error`. Comma-separated (`status=online,error`) or repeated (`status[]=online&status[]=error`).
- `effective_status` — optional, one or more of `ok`, `warning`, `error`, `offline`, `disconnected`, `never_seen`. Same list forms as `status`. Status filters can trail the live `status` by up to a minute.
- `model_id` — optional, device model id (UUID).
- `connection_method` — optional, one of `native`, `c2c`, `edge`.
- `connector_id` — optional, the cloud connector (C2C integration) or Edge id (UUID) — the `connector.id` of a device.

All filters combine with AND.

## Errors
> **Behavior change:** unknown query parameters used to be ignored. They are now rejected with `422`, so drop any extra parameter (a cache-buster, a `sort=`) your requests still send.

**422 Unprocessable Entity** — an unsupported query parameter, or an invalid filter value:
```json
{ "error": "Unsupported query parameter(s): foo. Supported: page, per_page, space_id, name, status, effective_status, model_id, connection_method, connector_id" }
```
```json
{ "error": "Invalid status: sleeping. status must be one or more of the following: offline / online / unavailable / error" }
```
`model_id` / `connector_id` that are not UUIDs are rejected with `"<param> must be a valid UUID"`.

## Success
**200 OK** — paginated list of devices.
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "c66308c8-1d12-...",
      "name": "Digital Media Player 2",
      "sn": "Q3RzbMS8-...",
      "mac": null,
      "cloud_id": "...",
      "status": "online",
      "effective_status": "ok",
      "merged_effective_status": "ok",
      "last_seen_at": "2024-07-24T07:22:20.037Z",
      "details": null,
      "model": { "id": "...", "name": "Digital Media Player", "sub_model": null },
      "firmware": { "version": "1.0.0" },
      "space": { "id": 17517, "full_path": "Green Energy Corp/France/Paris Demo Conference Room" },
      "connector": { "type": "c2c", "id": "5b1f0c2e-7a4d-...", "name": "Poly Lens" },
      "maintenance": {
        "manual": { "active": true, "source": "space" },
        "scheduled": { "active": false, "until": null }
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_page": 2
}
```
### Status fields
- `status` — the device's own raw self-reported state (`online` / `offline` / `unavailable` / `error`).
- `effective_status` — the device's own computed status: one of `ok`, `offline`, `error`, `warning`, `disconnected`, `never_seen`.
- `merged_effective_status` — merge-aware rollup of `effective_status` across the device group (primary + merged shadows), maintained on the group primary's row. On every other row — standalone or merged shadow — it mirrors that device's own `effective_status`.

### Maintenance
- `maintenance.manual.active` — the device is in manual maintenance (its own incidents snoozed, or its space in maintenance).
- `maintenance.manual.source` — `device_snooze` when the device's own snooze is active, else `space` when its space is in maintenance, else `null`.
- `maintenance.scheduled.active` — a scheduled maintenance window covers the device's space now (see Maintenance Schedules); `maintenance.scheduled.until` is when it ends, `null` when none is active. Indication only: it does not change `status` or `effective_status`.

### Connector
- `connector.type` — how the device connects: `native`, `c2c` (cloud connector) or `edge`.
- `connector.id` — the cloud connector or Edge id; `null` for native devices.
- `connector.name` — the cloud connector's display name (e.g. `Poly Lens`), or the Edge display name; `null` for native devices.

endpoints.title: Get Histories
endpoints.description:
## Query parameters
- `from` / `to` — Unix epoch seconds. Defaults: `from` = 1 week ago, `to` = now.
  The time window between `from` and `to` must not exceed **31 days**.
- `page` / `per_page` — pagination (defaults 1 / 100, `per_page` max 1000).
- `status` — filters by the device's *current* status (`online`, `offline`, `unavailable`, `error`), not the status recorded in each history row.
- `device_id`, `space_id`, `name` — optional filters.

## Success
**200 OK** — `items` plus `has_next_page` (boolean). No total count is returned.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — Invalid params, e.g. a `from`/`to` window wider than 31 days.

endpoints.title: Update Device
endpoints.description: `sn` and `mac` are accepted only when the device model allows editing them (the partner's "Allow org users to edit serial number" / "Allow org users to edit MAC address" model settings). `custom_model_name` and `custom_vendor_name` can be changed only on devices that connect through a C2C integration or an Edge; on devices that connect directly to Xyte they are defined by the device model and are rejected. Sending a field with its current value is not an edit. A rejected field fails the whole request with `422 Unprocessable Entity` and nothing is updated. The example body assumes an editable C2C or Edge device model.

endpoints.title: Change Model
endpoints.description:
Moves an edge device to another edge device model of the same vendor in place, for example from a Heartbeat model to the full driver for the same hardware. The device keeps its id, space and incidents; only its monitoring template and parameters change. Data collected by the previous model's template is discarded.

## Parameters
- `device_model_id` (required) — The target edge device model.
- `custom_parameters` (optional) — Object of parameter name to value for the target model, same as Start Claim. Current values of parameters the target model also declares are kept unless given here.
- `custom_model_name` (optional) — Model name shown for the device. When omitted, a device still showing the previous model's name is renamed to the target model's name; any other name is kept.

## Success
**200 OK**
```json
{
  "id": "device-id",
  "previous_device_model_id": "model-id",
  "device_model_id": "model-id",
  "custom_model_name": "Model name",
  "missing_parameters": ["{$PASSWORD}"],
  "edge_update": {
    "status": "update_sent",
    "edge_version": "1.3.10",
    "latest_edge_version": "2.1.1"
  }
}
```
`missing_parameters` lists the target model's parameters that are still empty. The driver may not collect data until they are set.

When the device's Edge is older than the latest Edge release, the Edge is sent its Update Version command and the device is moved without waiting for it; the driver starts collecting once the Edge runs the new version. `edge_update.status` is one of:
- `up_to_date` — The Edge already runs the latest release.
- `update_sent` — An Edge update was sent.
- `update_in_progress` — An Edge update was already running, so none was sent.
- `update_not_sent` — The Edge is behind, but its update could not be sent (for example, the Edge model has no Update Version command or it needs a license). Update the Edge yourself.
- `unknown_version` — The Edge's version or the latest release is unknown, so the Edge was not updated.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**404 Not Found** — Device not found in the organization.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — The device is not an edge device; the target is not an edge model of the device's vendor; the device is already on the target model; `custom_parameters` contains a parameter the target model does not declare or an invalid value; or the monitoring service for the Edge couldn't be reached, in which case the device is unchanged and the call can be retried.

endpoints.title: Get Claim Status
endpoints.description:
## Success
**200 OK**
```json
{
    "result": "success"
}
```
Possible `result` values depend on the claim state returned by Zabbix.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — `device_ip` not found or claim not initiated.

endpoints.title: Get Ping Status
endpoints.description:
## Success
**200 OK**
```json
{
    "status": "online"
}
```
Possible `status` values depend on the ping result returned by Zabbix.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — `device_ip` not found or ping not initiated.

endpoints.title: Start Claim
endpoints.description:
## Success
**204 No Content** — Claim process started successfully. No response body.

## Optional fields
- `mac` — MAC address of the device. Accepted in any common format (e.g. `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`, `AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF`, `aabbccddeeff`); it is normalized to `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff` before being stored.
- `sn` — Serial number to assign to the device. When omitted, the device's serial defaults to its generated UUID.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — Invalid parameters (e.g. unknown `device_model_id`, unreachable `device_ip`, malformed `mac`).

{
    "proxy_id": "",
    "device_model_id": "",

endpoints.title: Start Ping
endpoints.description:
## Success
**204 No Content** — Ping process started successfully. No response body.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — Invalid `device_ip` or unreachable proxy.

endpoints.title: Update Hostname
endpoints.description:
Updates the IP address or hostname an edge device is reachable on. The new address is synced to the monitoring server and stored on the device. The device's custom parameter values are preserved.

Unless `skip_connectivity_check` is `true`, a successful connectivity check for the new address must be performed first (see Start Ping / Get Ping Status).

## Success
**200 OK** — `{ "success": true }`

## Errors
**400 Bad Request** — Missing `device_ip`, or the new address has not passed a connectivity check.
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**404 Not Found** — Device not found in the organization.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — Malformed `device_ip` (must contain only letters, digits, dots, and hyphens).

endpoints.title: Get Incidents
endpoints.description:
## Query parameters
- `page` — page number (default `1`).
- `per_page` — results per page (default `100`, **max `500`**). Values above `500` are rejected with `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
- `from` / `to` — Unix timestamps (seconds) bounding the incident's `created_at`, inclusive. Default: the last week up to now.
- `status` — optional, `active` or `closed`; filters on the stored status. A snoozed incident reads `"status": "snoozed"` but is matched by `status=active` — use `snoozed=true` / `false` to pick snoozed incidents in or out.
- `priority` — optional, `critical`, `high`, `moderate`, `low` or `planning`.
- `title`, `description`, `issue`, `device_model`, `partner_name`, `sub_model` — optional, case-insensitive substring match.
- `space_id` — optional, only incidents on devices in this space.
- `notified` — optional, `true` / `false`: only incidents whose opening notification did (or did not) reach at least one of the organization's integrations.
- `with_notifications` — optional, `true` adds `notified` and `notifications` to every item (default `false`, which leaves the payload as it always was).
- `in_maintenance` — optional, `true` / `false`: only incidents that are (or are not) in maintenance mode.
- `snoozed` — optional, `true` / `false`: only incidents that are (or are not) snoozed — active with `snoozed_until` in the future, the rows that read `"status": "snoozed"`. An expired snooze, or a closed incident that still carries one, counts as not snoozed.
- `include_suppressed` — optional, `true` also returns the incidents suppressed by a scheduled maintenance window (default `false`).

> **Behavior change:** incidents suppressed by a scheduled maintenance window are no longer listed by default, matching the Xyte portal. Pass `include_suppressed=true` to get them back.

## Pagination
Results are sorted by `created_at` ascending (oldest first), ties broken by incident id, so the order is stable across pages. Keep following `next_page` until it is `null`. Pass explicit `from` and `to` and reuse the same values for every page: both default relative to the time of each request, so a window left to the defaults moves between calls and records at page boundaries get skipped.

## Success
**200 OK** — paginated list of incidents.
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "uuid": "7f7c3a52-0f3e-...",
      "status": "active",
      "priority": "high",
      "title": "Device offline",
      "description": "Device has not reported for 10 minutes",
      "device_id": "c66308c8-1d12-...",
      "device_name": "Digital Media Player 2",
      "device_model": "Digital Media Player",
      "device_sub_model": null,
      "partner_name": "Acme AV",
      "space_id": 17517,
      "space_tree_path_name": "Green Energy Corp/France/Paris Demo Conference Room",
      "space_name": "Paris Demo Conference Room",
      "issue": "offline",
      "space_incident": false,
      "created_at": "2026-08-26T08:23:14Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-26T08:23:14Z",
      "in_maintenance": false,
      "entered_maintenance_at": null,
      "snoozed_until": null,
      "scheduled_maintenance": {
        "suppressed": false,
        "suppressed_until": null,
        "announced_at": null
      },
      "notified": true,
      "notifications": [
        {
          "integration_id": "5f1c0d2e-7c3a-4b8e-9d21-...",
          "integration_type": "service_now",
          "status": "sent",
          "action": "create",
          "notified_at": "2026-08-26T08:23:18Z",
          "external_id": "46b66a40db98330010b6a0b5ca961905",
          "external_reference": "INC0010042",
          "external_url": "https://acme.service-now.com/nav_to.do?uri=incident.do?sys_id=46b66a40db98330010b6a0b5ca961905",
          "reason": null
        },
        {
          "integration_id": "9a7d4c11-2e5f-4f0b-8c3d-...",
          "integration_type": "email",
          "status": "skipped",
          "action": "create",
          "notified_at": null,
          "external_id": null,
          "external_reference": null,
          "external_url": null,
          "reason": "priority_filter"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "next_page": 2,
  "has_next_page": true,
  "total_count": 815
}
```
- `next_page` — the next page number, or `null` on the last page.
- `has_next_page` — `true` while more pages follow.
- `total_count` — how many incidents match the filters across all pages.

### Notification state (`with_notifications=true`)
`notified` and `notifications` appear only when asked for (the example above shows them). One `notifications` entry per organization integration the incident was dispatched to; `notified` is `true` once the opening notification reached at least one of them.
- `integration_type` — the integration driver (`service_now`, `jira`, `freshdesk`, `slack`, `msteams`, `email`, `web_hook`, ...).
- `status` / `reason` / `notified_at` / `external_*` describe the opening notification; later updates and closes do not change them. An update or close of an incident whose opening notification was never recorded records nothing.
- `status` — `sent` / `failed` / `skipped`; `action` — the last incident event dispatched to the integration: `create` / `update` / `close`.
- `notified_at` — when the opening notification was delivered; `null` until it is (a delivered close alone never sets it).
- `external_id` / `external_reference` / `external_url` — the record created on the integration's side: ServiceNow `sys_id` + number + link, Jira issue id, Freshdesk ticket id + link, ConnectWise ticket id, FreshService request number, Salesforce case id, Slack message `ts` + channel.
- `reason` — why it was not sent: for `failed`, `no_remote_reference` (`null` for a delivery error); for `skipped`, `priority_filter`, `integration_inactive`, `handler_declined`, `reference_already_present` (another integration of the same ticketing type - ServiceNow, Jira, Freshdesk, ConnectWise or FreshService - had already opened the incident's ticket on that system).

Recorded from the release of this feature onward: older incidents answer `"notified": false` with an empty list.

## Maintenance and snooze
`status=active` also returns incidents in maintenance mode and snoozed incidents (a snoozed one reads `"status": "snoozed"`) unless they are filtered out.
- `in_maintenance` — `true` while the incident is in maintenance mode (its device or space is under maintenance); `entered_maintenance_at` — when it entered maintenance, `null` when not in maintenance.
- `snoozed_until` — when the snooze ends, `null` when not set; the incident is snoozed only while this is in the future.
- On a room incident (`space_incident: true`), `in_maintenance` is the room row's own flag, not its member devices'.
- To match the Active tab of the organization portal, pass `status=active&in_maintenance=false&snoozed=false&from=0&to=<now>`. The portal has no time window, while `from` defaults to one week ago; fix `to` once and reuse it on every page, as described under Pagination.

### Scheduled maintenance
- `scheduled_maintenance.suppressed` — `true` while the incident is hidden because it opened inside a scheduled maintenance window (see Maintenance Schedules). A suppressed incident closed before the window ends stays suppressed.
- `scheduled_maintenance.suppressed_until` — when the window hiding it ends; `null` when not suppressed.
- `scheduled_maintenance.announced_at` — when a suppressed incident still open at the end of its window was announced as a new incident; `null` otherwise.

## Room incidents
When an organization has room incident grouping enabled, an outage of several devices in one room is returned as **one row** — the room incident — and its per-device member incidents are not listed.

- `space_incident` — `true` on a room incident, `false` on an ordinary device incident.
- On a room incident, `space_id` / `space_name` / `space_tree_path_name` describe the room, `issue` is `space_offline`, the title reads `Room offline: <room> (n of N devices)`, and `device_*` describe the first device that went offline.
- `issue=offline` also matches `space_offline`, since the filter is a substring match.

endpoints.title: Get Licenses
endpoints.description:
## Query parameters
All filters are optional and are combined with AND. Invalid values are rejected with `422 Unprocessable Entity`.

- `page` — page number (default `1`).
- `per_page` — results per page (default `100`, **max `100`**). Values above `100` are rejected with `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
- `state` — **multi-value**: repeat the key (`state[]=available&state[]=inuse`) or pass a comma-separated list (`state=available,inuse`). Allowed values: `available`, `inuse`, `remove`, `error`, `disabled`, `renew`. Any other value is rejected.
- `assigned` — `true` / `false`. `true` returns licenses linked to a device **or** pre-bound to a serial number (`bound_device_sn`); `false` returns licenses with neither. It says nothing about the device's claim state.
- `device_id` — exact match, licenses assigned to that device.
- `product_id` — exact match on the license's product.
- `device_model_id` — exact match on the license's device model.
- `bound_device_sn` — exact match on the serial number the license is pre-bound to.
- `warranty` — `true` / `false`, whether the license is a warranty license.
- `transferable` — `true` / `false`, whether the license can be moved to another device.
- `expires_before` / `expires_after` — ISO-8601 datetime compared against `expires_at` (inclusive), e.g. `2026-01-31T23:59:59Z`. A value without a UTC offset is interpreted as UTC. Licenses without an expiry (`"expires_at": null`) are excluded by either filter.
- `order_short_id` — exact match on the short id of the order the license was purchased under.

Results are always sorted by `created_at` descending (ties broken by `id`); the sort order is not client-configurable.

## States
Beyond the six filterable values above, a response may also contain the internal transitional state `disable` (a license on its way to `disabled`). It is not accepted as a `state` filter value.

## Success
**200 OK** — paginated list of licenses. `next_page` is the next page number, or `null` on the last page.
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "3f6b1c5e-2f19-4c1a-9a41-1c0d9b2f7a84",
      "state": "inuse",
      "expires_at": "2026-07-31T23:59:59Z",
      "activated_at": "2025-06-30T09:12:44Z",
      "payment_interval": "yearly",
      "duration": 365,
      "warranty": false,
      "transferable": true,
      "bound_device_sn": null,
      "created_at": "2025-06-29T14:03:11Z",
      "order_short_id": "ORD-4K7Q2M",
      "partner": { "id": "8ac2...", "name": "Acme AV" },
      "device": { "id": "c66308c8-1d12-...", "sn": "Q3RzbMS8-..." },
      "product": { "id": "1f9d...", "name": "Device Monitoring" },
      "device_model": { "id": "7b21...", "name": "Digital Media Player" }
    }
  ],
  "next_page": 2
}
```
Fields:

- `payment_interval` — how the license was bought: `one_time`, `monthly`, `yearly` or `usage_based` (billed monthly).
- `duration` — the license term in days (`30` monthly and usage-based, `365` yearly, `21915` — 60 years — one-time, the coverage term for a one-time warranty).
- `expires_at` — a hard cut-off, not the billing period. For `monthly` / `yearly` subscriptions it is the end of the paid period plus a 2-month billing grace period, and moves forward on every successful charge. `usage_based` licenses expire like `monthly` ones. `one_time` licenses expire about 100 years after purchase, i.e. effectively never.

Nullable fields:

- `device` — `null` for a license that is not assigned to a device. A license matched by `assigned=true` with `"device": null` is pre-bound to the serial number in `bound_device_sn`.
- `device_model` — comes from the purchased product, so it is populated whether or not the license is assigned to a device; `null` only when the product has no device model.
- `product` — `null` when the license is not linked to a product.
- `order_short_id` — `null` when the license was not created through a purchase.
- `payment_interval` — `null` when the license was not created through a purchase.
- `duration` — `null` only on older licenses created outside the store purchase flow; every store purchase records it.

endpoints.title: Create Maintenance Schedule
endpoints.description:
Creates a recurring maintenance window on the space in the path. It applies to the space and every space below it.

## Body
- `days` — required, one or more of `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun`: the weekdays the window starts on.
- `start` — required, `HH:MM` (`00:00`–`23:59`), local time in the space's timezone.
- `end` — required, `HH:MM` (`00:00`–`24:00`). An `end` at or before `start` runs into the next day; `00:00`–`24:00` is the whole day. `end` must differ from `start`.
- `name` — optional, up to 255 characters.
- `enabled` — optional, default `true`.

A space holds at most 10 schedules. The space comes from the path only; a schedule cannot be moved to another space.

## Success
**200 OK** — the schedule, in the shape of an item of Get Maintenance Schedules.

## Errors
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — a missing field, an unknown day, a malformed time, `start` equal to `end`, or an 11th schedule on the space:
```json
{ "error": "days must be among mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun" }
```
```json
{ "error": "Space cannot have more than 10 maintenance schedules" }
```
**404 Not Found** — no such space in the organization.

endpoints.title: Delete Maintenance Schedule
endpoints.description:
Deletes the schedule. The incidents it was hiding that are still open are announced as new incidents, unless another window still covers their space.

## Success
**200 OK**
```json
{ "success": true }
```

## Errors
**404 Not Found** — no such schedule in the organization.

endpoints.title: Get Maintenance Schedules
endpoints.description:
Lists the organization's recurring maintenance windows. An incident opened on a device while a window covers its space is suppressed: it stays on the device but is left out of incident lists, counts and integrations, and is announced as a new incident if it is still open when the window ends. Windows set on a space apply to every space below it.

## Query parameters
- `page` — page number (default `1`).
- `per_page` — results per page (default `100`, **max `100`**).
- `space_id` — optional, only the schedules set on this space (not the ones it inherits).
- `enabled` — optional, `true` / `false`.
- `active_now` — optional, `true` / `false`: whether the schedule's own window covers the current time. A disabled schedule is never active.

## Success
**200 OK** — paginated list of schedules, oldest first.
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "3c1e2f4a-8b7d-4c6e-9f10-...",
      "name": "Nightly",
      "days": ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri"],
      "start": "02:00",
      "end": "06:00",
      "enabled": true,
      "space": { "id": 17517, "name": "Paris Office", "path": "Green Energy Corp/France/Paris Office" },
      "active_now": false,
      "until": null,
      "next_start_at": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z",
      "next_end_at": "2026-10-21T04:00:00Z",
      "created_by": { "id": "9d2b6a10-...", "name": "Jane Doe" },
      "created_at": "2026-10-20T09:12:44Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-10-20T09:12:44Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_page": null,
  "total_count": 1
}
```
- `days` — the weekdays the window starts on: `mon` … `sun`.
- `start` / `end` — local wall-clock time `HH:MM` in the timezone of the schedule's space (falling back to its customer space, then UTC). An `end` at or before `start` runs into the next day; `00:00`–`24:00` is the whole day.
- `active_now` — the schedule's own window covers the current time.
- `until` — when the schedule's current window ends (UTC) while `active_now` is true, `null` otherwise.
- `next_start_at` / `next_end_at` — the next window of this schedule that starts after now (UTC), `null` when none starts within 7 days.
- `created_by` — the user who signed in for the OAuth token that created it; `null` when created with an API key.
- `total_count` — how many schedules match the filters across all pages.

endpoints.title: Get Space Maintenance Schedules
endpoints.description:
The schedules that apply to a space: the ones set on it, the enabled ones it inherits from its ancestors, and the resulting coverage.

## Success
**200 OK**
```json
{
  "own": [
    {
      "id": "3c1e2f4a-8b7d-4c6e-9f10-...",
      "name": "Nightly",
      "days": ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat", "sun"],
      "start": "02:00",
      "end": "06:00",
      "enabled": true,
      "space": { "id": 17520, "name": "Boardroom", "path": "Green Energy Corp/France/Paris Office/Boardroom" },
      "active_now": true,
      "until": "2026-10-20T04:00:00Z",
      "next_start_at": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z",
      "next_end_at": "2026-10-21T04:00:00Z",
      "created_by": null,
      "created_at": "2026-10-20T09:12:44Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-10-20T09:12:44Z"
    }
  ],
  "inherited": [
    {
      "schedule": {
        "id": "7a4d0b9e-1c2f-4e3a-8b5d-...",
        "name": "Weekly update",
        "days": ["sun"],
        "start": "05:00",
        "end": "08:00",
        "enabled": true,
        "space": { "id": 17517, "name": "Paris Office", "path": "Green Energy Corp/France/Paris Office" },
        "active_now": false,
        "until": null,
        "next_start_at": "2026-10-25T04:00:00Z",
        "next_end_at": "2026-10-25T07:00:00Z",
        "created_by": null,
        "created_at": "2026-10-01T10:00:00Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-10-01T10:00:00Z"
      },
      "from_space": { "id": 17517, "name": "Paris Office" }
    }
  ],
  "effective": {
    "active": true,
    "until": "2026-10-20T04:00:00Z",
    "next_start_at": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```
- `own` — every schedule set on this space, enabled or not.
- `inherited` — the enabled schedules set on its ancestors; `from_space` is the ancestor carrying it.
- `effective` — the union of all enabled windows covering the space. Overlapping or touching windows chain into one. `until` is when the current window ends (`null` when none is active); `next_start_at` is the next window start after now, `null` beyond 7 days.

## Errors
**404 Not Found** — no such space in the organization.

endpoints.title: Update Maintenance Schedule
endpoints.description:
Partial update: send only the fields to change — `name`, `days`, `start`, `end`, `enabled`, with the same rules as Create Maintenance Schedule.

Disabling, shortening or deleting a window releases the incidents it was hiding right away: each one still open is announced as a new incident, unless another window still covers its space.

## Success
**200 OK** — the updated schedule, in the shape of an item of Get Maintenance Schedules.

## Errors
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — an unknown day, a malformed time, or a change that makes `start` equal `end`.
**404 Not Found** — no such schedule in the organization.

## Maintenance
Every space carries a `maintenance` object:
```json
"maintenance": {
  "manual": { "active": true, "inherited": true },
  "scheduled": {
    "active": true,
    "until": "2026-10-21T04:00:00Z",
    "next_start_at": "2026-10-22T00:00:00Z",
    "has_schedules": false,
    "inherits_schedules": true
  }
}
```
- `manual.active` — the space is in manual maintenance; `manual.inherited` — `true` when that comes from an ancestor put in maintenance rather than this space itself.
- `scheduled.active` — a scheduled maintenance window (see Maintenance Schedules) covers the space now; `scheduled.until` is when the covering window ends, `scheduled.next_start_at` the next window start after now (`null` beyond 7 days). Indication only: it does not change the room status.
- `scheduled.has_schedules` — enabled schedules are set on this space; `scheduled.inherits_schedules` — an enabled schedule on an ancestor applies to it.

## Maintenance filters
- `maintenance_scheduled_active` — optional, `true`: only spaces a scheduled maintenance window covers now; `false`: only the others.

Create User
endpoints.description:
## Success
**200 OK** — the created user, plus the outcome of the invitation email.
```json
{
  "id": "9e34b87d-79ca-4dc3-ac42-8ce9ebe8be82",
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "group_names": ["administrators"],
  "deactivated_at": null,
  "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z",
  "welcome_email_status": "failed",
  "message": "The user was created, but we couldn't send the invitation email. Please try Resend Signup Email later."
}
```
- `welcome_email_status` — how the invitation email went:
  - `sent` — the welcome email with the sign-in link was sent.
  - `sso` — the organization enforces single sign-on, so the user was sent an email to sign in with their company account instead.
  - `failed` — the user was created, but the invitation email could not be sent. Retry with **Resend Welcome Email**.
- `message` — a human-readable notice, present only when `welcome_email_status` is `sso` or `failed`.

A failed invitation does **not** fail the request: the user exists either way, so check `welcome_email_status` rather than the HTTP status.

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — Missing `email`, `name` or `group_ids`, an invalid email, or an email already associated with another account.

endpoints.title: Resend Welcome Email
endpoints.description:
## Success
**200 OK**
```json
{ "message": "Email sent" }
```
`message` is `"Email sent"` when the welcome email with the sign-in link was sent. When the organization enforces single sign-on, the user is sent an email to sign in with their company account instead, and `message` is an informational notice saying so:
```json
{ "message": "Your organization uses single sign-on, so we sent them an email to sign in with their company account." }
```

## Errors
**401 Unauthorized** — Missing or invalid `Authorization` header.
**403 Forbidden** — `User already confirmed`: the user has already confirmed their account, so there is no welcome email to resend.
**404 Not Found** — The user does not exist, does not belong to this organization, or is deactivated.
**422 Unprocessable Entity** — `We couldn't send the invitation email. Please try again later.`: the email could not be sent.

endpoints.title: Get Device Info
endpoints.description:
## Success
**200 OK** — the requested device.
```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "....-03cfda750cfa",
      "sn": "123",
      "mac": "11:00:00:00:00:00",
      "cloud_id": "....",
      "status": null,
      "effective_status": "ok",
      "merged_effective_status": "ok",
      "last_seen_at": "2022-11-06T09:52:47.546Z",
      "details": {},
      "state": {},
      "claimed": "Acme Inc",
      "model": { "id": "....-d75e0abec7d2", "name": "model name", "sub_model": "sub model" },
      "firmware": { "version": "1.0.1" }
    }
  ]
}
```
### Status fields
- `status` — the device's own raw self-reported state (`online` / `offline` / `error`).
- `effective_status` — the device's own computed status: one of `ok`, `offline`, `error`, `warning`, `disconnected`, `never_seen`.
- `merged_effective_status` — merge-aware rollup of `effective_status` across the device group (primary + merged shadows), maintained on the group primary's row. On every other row — standalone or merged shadow — it mirrors that device's own `effective_status`.
